summary: This article explains how fossils form when ancient plants and animals are buried and slowly turned to rock, and what they teach us about life long ago, including in Saudi Arabia's own deserts.
introduce: Show the title “Fossils: Clues from Ancient Life” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: kept safe from damage or decay for a long time
a natural, non-living solid substance found in rock or soil
one flat level of material lying on top of or under another

challengeTerms.def: turned into stone as minerals slowly replace an organism's original material
to dig up something carefully, usually for scientific study
a layer or structure of rock that built up over a long period of time

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a desert that has no water today could still hold proof that it was once covered by a sea? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why fossils of ancient elephants found in the Nafud desert are an important clue.
struggling: Pre-teach preserved, mineral, and layer with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses petrified, excavate, and formation to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
